cohort.definition: Students and recent graduates entering Stripe as software engineers, anchored on the firm's published Software Engineer, Intern listing — the clearest official statement of the entry screen. Experienced hires are a separate cohort.
cohort.time_window: listing live on Stripe's careers site when checked, October 2026

compensation_notes.statement: Stripe publishes an annual salary range on many role listings and states on them that the range may span several career levels and is narrowed during the interview process based on experience, qualifications and location, with equity, bonus and benefits on top. The intern listing checked for this record is the authoritative source for that role's own terms.

data_sources.label: Stripe official job listing: Software Engineer, Intern — minimum requirements and preferred qualifications
Stripe official careers search (open roles), checked October 2026
Stripe official job listing (Strategic Capacity Planning Specialist) — the firm's published pay-range and in-office-expectation language

entry_routes.accessibility_note: The published entry door: the listing's minimum requirements are a real screen — CS fundamentals through a degree in progress, programming evidence from projects or classwork, and prior multi-person project experience.
entry_routes.route: Software Engineer, Intern (converts to new-grad offers)

entry_routes.accessibility_note: The listing explicitly counts open-source contributions as qualifying multi-person project experience — a route fully open to students at any school.
entry_routes.route: Open-source / multi-person project route into the same screen

entry_routes.accessibility_note: Stripe's engineering hiring is team-posted rather than one annual cohort; adjacent teams' new-grad postings run on the same stated screens.
entry_routes.route: New-grad software engineer postings across product and infrastructure teams

hiring_bar_summary.statement: Stripe publishes its intern bar in the listing itself: strong CS fundamentals through pursuit of a Bachelor's or Master's in computer science, math or a related discipline; programming experience from side projects or classwork; and experience in previous internships or other multi-person projects — including open source — that shows you can take feedback from mentors, peers and stakeholders.

hiring_cadence.statement: A Software Engineer, Intern listing was live on Stripe's careers site when checked in October 2026. Stripe posts roles as teams open them; there is no single published annual application date on the sources checked, so the careers search is the live source of truth.

interview_styles.statement: The listing's preferred qualifications signal the interview's center of gravity: high-quality pull requests with good test coverage, work in unfamiliar codebases across multiple languages, and clear written communication about your work. This record found no official public page detailing Stripe's interview rounds, and invents none.

known_biases_of_data: No population sample exists for this record: Stripe publishes requirements, not who passes them. Every distribution below restates the published screen qualitatively; none of it is a measured hire mix.

A job listing is the firm's stated ideal, written to attract applicants — it understates how much school brand and referrals may matter in practice, which this record cannot measure from public sources.
The intern listing checked is one posting; team-specific listings vary in their preferred qualifications.

entries.label: Computer science, mathematics, or a related discipline
entries.note: This is the degree frame named in the official intern listing's minimum requirements — a stated screen, not a measured major mix of hires.

path_patterns.pattern: Intern first, convert: the intern listing is written as the entry door, with prior internships or multi-person projects as the evidence it asks for
Project-evidence route: side projects and open-source contributions are named in the listing itself as qualifying programming and collaboration evidence

entries.label: Prior internships or multi-person projects, including open source
entries.note: Stated in the official listing as minimum-requirement evidence — experience of evaluating and receiving feedback from mentors, peers and stakeholders. It is a requirement pattern, not a measured employer mix.

process_stages.description: Apply against a listing whose minimum and preferred qualifications are published in full; the screen described here is that published text, nothing more.

red_flags.statement: Stripe's listings state an in-office expectation (at least half of working time in the local office for office-assigned roles in most locations). Candidates who need fully remote work should treat that as a real term, not boilerplate.

The current intern listing expects candidates to leverage AI tools while applying rigorous critical thinking to review and validate outputs — submitting unreviewed AI output as your own work is exactly the failure mode the listing warns about.

referral_weight_notes.statement: No official statement on referral weight appears in the sources checked for this record. The listing's screens are evidence-based (projects, pull requests, writing), so the defensible assumption is that a referral may open a conversation but the artifacts still carry the decision.

entries.label: No school pattern published
entries.note: Stripe publishes no school distribution for its hires, and the intern listing names no schools. This record states no school pattern rather than guessing one.

revealed.statement: Revealed by the listing's own preferred list: the ability to write clearly about your work to stakeholders and teammates is screened as an engineering skill at Stripe, not a soft extra.
Revealed by the same list: comfort navigating unfamiliar, multi-language codebases and shipping pull requests with test coverage — craft evidence over pedigree.

stated.statement: Minimum: CS fundamentals via a Bachelor's or Master's in progress in CS, math or a related field; programming familiarity from side projects or classwork — Stripe mainly works in Ruby, Java, JavaScript, Go and Scala, and states new languages can be learned when fundamentals are present.

Preferred: at least 1 year of university education or equivalent experience; one or more areas of specialized knowledge balanced with general skills; experience from previous internships or multi-person projects including open source.

entries.label: Ruby, Java, JavaScript, Go, Scala
entries.note: The languages the official intern listing names as Stripe's main working set — a stated environment, with the listing adding that new languages can be learned if fundamentals are present.

entries.label: Clear written communication
entries.note: Named in the listing's preferred qualifications: writing clearly to explain your work to stakeholders, team members and other Stripes.

entries.label: Pull-request craft and test coverage
entries.note: Named in the listing's preferred qualifications: high-quality pull requests with good test coverage, completing projects with minimal defects.

entries.label: AI tools, used with critical judgment
entries.note: The listing expects interns to leverage AI tools to accelerate development while rigorously reviewing, refining and validating all outputs.

thesis_text: Stripe is unusually legible: its intern listing publishes the actual screen. Fundamentals from a CS or math degree in progress, programming evidence from projects or classwork, and prior experience working on multi-person projects — open source explicitly counts. The revealed tilt is craft: clear written communication, clean pull requests with tests, and comfort in unfamiliar codebases matter as much as raw algorithm speed. No population data on who gets in is published, so this record is qualitative throughout and states no school or major shares.

values_culture_signals.statement: The intern listing itself asks for the ability to learn unfamiliar systems through independent research and work with mentors and subject-matter experts — a user-and-craft orientation stated in the requirements, not just the marketing pages.
